offgrid_check.title: ⚠️ Off-Grid Inverter Safety Check
offgrid_check.description:
**CRITICAL SAFETY CHECK**

Do you have an Off-Grid inverter (SPF series)?

Off-Grid inverters will experience a POWER RESET if auto-detection is attempted.

• If YES: You will manually select your model (safe)
• If NO: Automatic detection will proceed (safe for grid-tied models)

Examples of Off-Grid models: SPF 3000-6000 ES PLUS

data_description.has_offgrid: Enable this ONLY if you have an SPF series off-grid inverter. Off-Grid inverters use a different protocol and will reset if VPP registers are accessed.

init.title: Growatt Modbus Options
init.description: Configure device name, inverter profile, polling settings, and grid power options

data_description.device_name: Friendly name for the device (appears before all sensor names)
data_description.inverter_series: Select your inverter model/series (auto-selects protocol version)
data_description.scan_interval: How often to poll the inverter when online (5-300 seconds)
data_description.offline_scan_interval: How often to poll when inverter is offline/at night (60-3600 seconds, default 300)
data_description.timeout: How long to wait for responses from the inverter (1-60 seconds)
data_description.invert_grid_power: Enable if CT clamp installed backwards (swaps import/export on AC side)
data_description.invert_battery_power: Enable if battery power shows opposite direction (inverts charge/discharge sign)
data_description.battery_voltage_range: Override automatic battery voltage register selection. Use High-voltage when VPP register 31214 does not respond and register 3169 reads ~10× too low (symptom of a 16-bit overflow on ARK/HV battery systems).
data_description.modbus_delay: Minimum pause between consecutive Modbus requests within a poll cycle (50–1000 ms, default 250). Increase to 500–1000 ms if the log shows transaction ID mismatch errors or if the inverter logs spurious fault entries while the integration is running.
data_description.device_path: Paths under /dev/serial/by-id/ are tied to the adapter itself and survive a reboot. A /dev/ttyUSB path is assigned in plug order and can move to a different device when you have more than one USB serial adapter.
data_description.manual_path: Overrides the selection above. Use this if the adapter is not listed, or to paste a /dev/serial/by-id/ path.
data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the RS485-to-TCP gateway.
data_description.max_block_size: Registers requested per Modbus read. Auto lets the profile decide. Lower this if entities are unavailable or stuck at zero and the log shows short reads or "Unable to decode request" - some RS485 gateways truncate large responses.
data_description.protocol_variant: Ten inverter families exist as two register maps - a V1.39 legacy one and a VPP V2.01 one. Auto uses whatever auto-detection concluded at setup and is right for almost everyone. Change it only if sensors that should work are reporting nothing: an inverter without VPP support on the V2.01 map cannot read the 30000/31000 range, and the reverse leaves the VPP sensors empty.

write_reversion.title: Growatt: settings are being reverted
write_reversion.description:
Local changes to **{controls}** were reverted shortly after being set, so the inverter is not keeping them.

The usual causes, in order of likelihood:

- **Growatt's cloud is pushing settings back.** A ShineWiFi or ShineLink dongle that is only uploading telemetry does not appear to be enough on its own — one user runs one alongside this integration with local writes persisting overnight. What overwrites local changes is the cloud sending settings *down*: remote control enabled in the ShinePhone app, or a schedule configured there. Turn those off before disconnecting anything.
- **A prerequisite setting is not enabled.** On MOD inverters, *Allow Grid Charge* must be Enabled before time-of-use schedules will persist.
- **The register is not writable on your firmware.** Some models accept the write and ignore it. The log has the register number if you want to report it.

This notice will not reappear until Home Assistant restarts.

unknown_profile.title: Growatt: inverter model no longer recognised
unknown_profile.description:
This entry is configured for the profile **{profile}**, which no longer exists in the integration.

It has fallen back to a MIN 7-10kW profile so Home Assistant can still start, but that profile reads different registers from your inverter. Most sensors will be missing or stuck at zero until this is corrected.

**Fix it:** go to Settings > Devices & Services > Growatt Modbus > Configure, and select your model.

The usual cause is a profile added or edited by hand in the integration's folder, which an update then replaced. If you need a model the integration does not cover, please open an issue rather than editing the files - a profile added properly survives updates.

gateway_malformed_frames.title: Growatt: RS485 gateway returning mismatched responses
gateway_malformed_frames.description:
The gateway at **{gateway}** answered **{percent}%** of requests with a frame that did not match the request — typically a complete response to an *earlier* request, replayed.

**Your data is not affected.** These responses are detected and discarded rather than decoded, which is what this check is for. But the reads are lost, so sensors update less often than they should.

This is a gateway problem, not an inverter problem. Things that have helped others:

- Set **Max Register Block Size** to 25 in the integration options.
- Check the gateway is in **Modbus TCP to RTU** mode, not transparent passthrough.
- If it has a TCP timeout setting, make sure it is enabled rather than disabled, so dead sessions are cleaned up.

See the linked guide for gateways known to work and the settings they use.

profile_mismatch.title: Growatt: this inverter may be on the wrong profile
profile_mismatch.description:
Your inverter reports device type code **{dtc}** ({model}), which indicates the **{suggested}** profile. The integration is currently using **{configured}**.

**Nothing has been changed, and your setup is working.** The profile in use creates **{configured_count} sensors**; the one your device type code indicates creates **{suggested_count}**. Compare that against your device page before deciding - if you are not missing anything you care about, there is nothing here you need to do.

Most often this follows a failed read during setup, where a single timed-out request left detection falling back to a best guess. It can also happen because one device type code covers several models, in which case the profile named here may be a sibling of yours rather than a better fit.

**To change it:** Settings → Devices & services → Growatt Modbus → Configure, and select **{suggested}**. Your entity IDs are preserved, so automations, dashboards and history carry over.

If the current profile is deliberate, or the suggested one behaves worse, please say so on GitHub - the device type code mapping may be wrong for your model and that is worth knowing.
